lines.en: What we remember is rarely what happened; it is the story we have told ourselves about what happened.
It is unsettling to realize that every time we recall a memory, we rewrite it a little.
Were our memories perfectly accurate, forgiveness would be much harder to find.
However old the wound, some anniversaries arrive with the weight of the first day.
Not until the last witness dies does an event fully pass from memory into history.
It is said that we are all unreliable narrators of our own lives.
What the old photograph preserves is not the moment, but the version of the moment someone chose to keep.
The smell of jasmine, for no reason he could name, returned him to his grandmother's balcony.
Little of what we learn at school survives, but the teacher who believed in us is never forgotten.
Rarely do two siblings remember the same childhood.
What the mind keeps of a whole year can sometimes be reduced to a single afternoon.
It is a mercy that memory fades; were every embarrassment perfectly preserved, none of us would leave the house.
Were we able to choose our memories, we would keep the wrong ones and delete the ones that taught us.
Not until the house was emptied did the family discover how many of its stories lived inside the furniture.
However vivid a memory feels, its details have been repainted by every retelling since.
